resources.string: Each group shows how recovered it is from your logged sets and the workouts your watch shares (runs, rides, hikes). Big muscles (legs, back) take about 3 days after a hard session, chest about 2.5, shoulders 2 and arms, calves and abs about 1.5; lighter sessions recover sooner. It is an estimate: how you feel counts too.
%1$d sets this week (10–20 is the range that builds muscle).
While they recover: an easy 20–30 minute walk, hip and ankle mobility, and stretching for quads and hamstrings. Skip hard runs and jumps until they are ready.
While it recovers: shoulder mobility, gentle stretching and light cardio. You can train legs or core meanwhile.
Arms and calves recover fast: light work or stretching now, and you can load them again in a day or two.
Abs handle frequent training, but give them a day after hard work. Breathing work, gentle planks and walking help.
Sleeping well and eating enough protein speed up recovery.

Notifies you when your watch records cardio on muscles that are still recovering, after a very long day of exercise, with too much weekly volume on a muscle, or after a week without rest. Works for gym and home training.

At the gym you get machines first. At home you get exercises with the equipment you have (dumbbells, bands, kettlebells) or your body weight. Coach can change this when you tell it where you are training.
No exercises for this muscle with your home equipment. Try body weight or add equipment in Coach.
